oil.summary: Crude staged a strong session with Brent clearing $93 — a three-week high — and WTI adding 1.15%, both supported by an increasingly fractured Middle East supply picture. Iranian oil exports have effectively hit zero, confirmed by the Iranian Central Bank, as sanctions and war conditions shut off flows entirely. Chinese state tankers are avoiding both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, amplifying logistical stress and pushing supertanker rates to record highs per the FT. Beijing is simultaneously redirecting Russian barrels away from India to replace lost Iranian volumes, reshuffling Asia-Pacific trade flows. ADNOC issued its ninth spot crude tender since June, signaling UAE is stepping up to fill the void. A temporary US easing of Russia oil sanctions, which has riled European allies, adds a wildcard to the supply narrative. The glaring outlier is RBOB gasoline, which collapsed 7.28% on the day — no headline explanation is available in today's feed. Heating Oil slipped 1.65% intraday but holds a solid monthly gain of 5.54%.
drivers: Iranian crude exports confirmed at zero by Iranian Central Bank, removing a meaningful supply source from global markets
Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab disruptions forcing Chinese state tankers to reroute, driving supertanker rates to all-time highs
RBOB gasoline crashed 7.28% intraday — a stark divergence from crude strength with no supporting headline available in today's feed

gas.summary: News flow for the US natural gas market is thin today — only one headline was available, covering China's dual-track energy strategy of expanding both renewables and fossil fuels simultaneously. Henry Hub slipped 1.81% on the day and is down 5.54% on the month, suggesting domestic fundamentals remain soft despite the broader energy market tension. European TTF, by contrast, surged 3.82% on the day and is up nearly 9% on the week, likely reflecting spillover from Middle East supply anxiety and Hormuz closure risks affecting LNG routing — though no Europe-specific gas headline was provided today. Traders should treat the HH/TTF divergence as a key spread to watch given the geopolitical backdrop.
drivers: Henry Hub down 1.81% on the day and 5.54% on the month, pointing to continued softness in US domestic gas fundamentals
TTF surging 3.82% intraday and +8.95% on the week, likely reflecting European anxiety over Middle East supply disruption and LNG rerouting risks

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs ticked up modestly, gaining 0.77% to $78.00 on the day but remain slightly soft over the past month at -0.95%, suggesting the carbon market has not yet fully priced in the geopolitical risk premium visible elsewhere in energy. The dominant input cost signal for European power is the TTF gas price, which jumped 3.82% today and is up nearly 9% on the week, putting upward pressure on gas-fired generation marginal costs and therefore power prices. Iran's continued insistence that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US meets its demands — headlines dated August 18 — sustains the risk-on tone for European energy broadly. Headline coverage specific to power and carbon is sparse today; the China renewables-versus-fossil-fuels story is the only sector-adjacent news available.
drivers: TTF gas up 3.82% on the day raises marginal cost of gas-fired power generation across Europe, indirectly supporting power prices
Strait of Hormuz closure, with Iran refusing to reopen until US meets demands, sustains elevated geopolitical risk premium across European energy markets
EUA carbon at $78.00 with only a 0.77% daily gain — carbon market appears to be lagging the broader energy risk move; sector-specific headline flow is thin today
